bant-01-c1.text: Schultheiss P, Nooten SS, Wang R, Wong MKL, Brassard F, Guénard B (2022). The abundance, biomass, and distribution of ants on Earth. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 119(40), e2201550119.
bant-01-c1.quote: estimate the number of all ants on Earth to be almost 20 × 10<sup>15</sup> individuals.
bant-01-c1.claim: Their answer, published in PNAS, was about 20 quadrillion ants, which is 20 followed by 15 zeros

bant-01-c1.text: Schultheiss P, Nooten SS, Wang R, Wong MKL, Brassard F, Guénard B (2022). The abundance, biomass, and distribution of ants on Earth. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 119(40), e2201550119.
bant-01-c1.quote: This exceeds the combined biomass of wild birds and mammals and is equivalent to ∼20% of human biomass.
bant-01-c1.claim: That's more than all wild birds and wild mammals combined, and about a fifth of the carbon in human bodies.

bant-01-c3.text: Hashemi S (2025). Scientists discover the oldest known ant fossil, a 113-million-year-old hell ant preserved in rock in Brazil. Smithsonian Magazine.
bant-01-c3.quote: The 113-million-year-old fossil of Vulcanidris cratensis is the first known hell ant preserved in rock rather than amber.
bant-01-c3.claim: The oldest known ant fossil, Vulcanidris cratensis, was described in 2025 from limestone of the Crato Formation in Brazil, about 113 million years old.

bant-01-c3.text: Hughes WOH, Oldroyd BP, Beekman M, Ratnieks FLW (2008). Ancestral monogamy shows kin selection is key to the evolution of eusociality. Science 320(5880), 1213-1216.
bant-01-c3.quote: a comparative analysis of female mating frequencies in 267 species of eusocial bees, wasps, and ants
bant-01-c3.claim: A 2008 study of 267 bee, wasp and ant species found that single mating was ancestral in all eight social lineages examined
